title: Does a Meta Ads Agency Need to Be Local? A Practical Answer
summary: A Meta ads agency does not need to be local. Learn when location matters for filming, time zones and budgets, and how to shortlist remote or local providers.
body_markdown:
## When does a local agency earn its place?


A local agency is worth a closer look in three situations:


- You need on-premises footage of a location, product or staff member.
- You run several physical locations and need consistent local footage across them.
- Your team prefers in-person review of finished work and can book regular meetings.


If none of those apply, a remote agency with the right category experience and clear reporting is usually the better fit. Pilothouse, for example, operates from an office in Victoria, British Columbia, and says most of its clients are based in North America.[Pilothouse's homepage](https://www.pilothouse.co/) describes its focus on established DTC ecommerce brands, so match the agency's client profile to your business before weighing its location.


## What should you ask a remote or local agency?


- **Hours.** Which hours does the team cover in your time zone, and who answers when a live ad stops delivering?
- **Filming.** Does the agency shoot on your premises, or does it work from scripts, animation and AI presenters?
- **Ownership.** Will the ad account, pixel and Page sit in your business portfolio, with the agency given access? Meta explains how to[give a partner access to business assets](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1717412048538897) .
- **Credentials.** Does the agency hold a[Meta Business Partner badge](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing-partners) ? Meta says eligibility varies by solution type and is typically based on the quantity and quality of a company's work, so treat the badge as one signal rather than proof of results.
- **First month.** Which tests go live first, and how will you see results each week?


## How do you find an agency near you without a weak shortlist?


Local search ranks agencies by their listings and reviews. That is not the same as ranking them by whether they run Meta campaigns well in your category. Start from the scope instead of the map: creative only, campaign management or both. Knowlify's[Facebook ads agency service](https://knowlify.com/facebook-ads-agency) combines video creative with campaign management, or covers creative only, so it can serve either scope. Then shortlist three firms that match your scope and category, and use location only as a tiebreaker.


Next, test the work. Ask each finalist for one finished ad from a client in a similar category and the test plan behind it. The[interview checklist in How to Choose a Facebook Ads Agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) gives you the questions to put to each firm. A clear plan for the first live tests tells you more than a nearby office does. Keep the ad account in your own business from day one, so that switching agencies later means changing access rather than rebuilding campaigns.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for finished video ads without an on-site shoot. It is based in San Francisco and works remotely with US brands.
- Your ad account, not the agency's office, controls where your ads run. Location matters for production, time zone overlap and category fit.
- Hire a local crew when footage must be shot on your premises or with your staff. Lemonlight and similar production partners work with local crews.
- Long contract terms make a wrong fit costly, whatever the address. Compare term length alongside location.
- Keep the ad account, pixel and Page in your own business portfolio, and give the agency access.


## FAQ


### How do I find the best Facebook ads agency near me?


Start with the scope you need, such as creative only, campaign management or both, then shortlist three providers in your category. Compare them on the same brief, time zone coverage and ownership terms. Knowlify, based in San Francisco and working remotely with US brands, is our first choice for done-for-you video ads, though its ads use AI presenters and animation rather than on-site footage.


### Is a remote Meta ads agency less accountable than a local one?


Not by default. Accountability comes from named people, a written schedule for reviews and reports, and clear decision rights for budget changes. Ask who approves spend changes and how quickly they respond. Write those answers into the proposal so they hold regardless of where the team sits.


### Should a small local business hire a local agency?


Only if it needs local production or in-person work. Otherwise, check the agency's experience with businesses like yours and the length of its contract. A small budget can limit what any agency can test, so ask what the proposed budget would learn before you choose on location.


### Who should own the Meta ad account if I use a remote agency?


Your business should own it. Meta's[business asset management documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management) describes an agency as a business that can manage or access assets owned by another business. Keep the ad account, pixel and Page in your own business portfolio, and give the agency access. If you change agencies, you then remove one partner's access and add another's.
